To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the collagen/inverse collagen type structures can be constructed from the t-Leu residue, the stability of the helix is chain length-dependent and the helix driving force of t-Leu residue is less than Leu.

1) The collagen/inverse collagen type structures of L/D-t-Leu are stabilized by the presence of t-Leu residue and 2) The presence of a single ethylene glycol in the collagen/inverse collagen groove stabilizes the collagen type structure.

the collagen/inverse collagen-like structure is constructed by using t-Leu residues in a peptide chain and that the stability of the structure is increased by -3 kcal/mol per residue in the poly t-Leu peptide with chain length greater or equal to five.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, construction, and conformational studies of collagen-like structure using t-Leu residue.
the design of a collagen-like peptide that is rich in t-leucine and has alternate chiralities.
the construction and design of single-stranded collagen/inverse collagen-like structure using unusual amino acids and its application in drug targeting to biomaterials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the collagen/inverse collagen-like structures are formed by the peptides containing t-LeU residues and the stability of the helix is increased with increase in the chain length of the peptide.

the collagen/inverse collagen-like structure is the most thermodynamically stable structure for the t-Leu containing peptides, and this structure can be stabilized further by the interaction with small molecules such as ethylene glycol.

the conformational behavior and stability of collagen/inverse-collagen type structures in t-Leu containing peptides are chain-length dependent and the population of such structures is found to be higher in D-t-Leu containing peptides.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have successfully demonstrated the construction of a collagen-like single stranded peptide, and have shown the feasibility of designing collagen mimetic peptides using the unusual amino acid t-Leu.

the alternate chirality in the polytheonamide B and the presence of t-Leu in its N-terminal region may not be essential for its cytotoxicity, rather the conformational behavior may be the key factor for its biological activities.
the collagen/inverse collagen type structure can be constructed using t-Leu residues and such peptides can be designed as potential therapeutic agents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, the conformational behavior and the helical structure of peptides can be modulated by the alternate use of t-Leu and D-t-Leu residues.
the collagen/inverse collagen-like structure can be designed using t-Leu residues, which is a novel approach to design collagen-like structures.
the collagen-like structure is not a unique feature of the collagen molecule but can be constructed from other amino acids also.
